problem_text:
A logistics firm must coordinate a circuit of 11 regional warehouses for a critical inventory audit:

Warehouse Alpha: Positioned at grid reference (11,48)
Warehouse Beta: Positioned at grid reference (94,20)
Warehouse Gamma: Positioned at grid reference (53,134)
Warehouse Delta: Positioned at grid reference (88,48)
Warehouse Epsilon: Positioned at grid reference (51,64)
Warehouse Zeta: Positioned at grid reference (172,186)
Warehouse Eta: Positioned at grid reference (188,77)
Warehouse Theta: Positioned at grid reference (79,132)
Warehouse Iota: Positioned at grid reference (98,65)
Warehouse Kappa: Positioned at grid reference (123,88)
Warehouse Lambda: Positioned at grid reference (182,61)

The transit distances between warehouses, measured in kilometers, are precisely known:
Alpha to Gamma: 95.7 km
Alpha to Delta: 77.0 km
Alpha to Epsilon: 43.1 km
Alpha to Zeta: 212.0 km

Gamma to Kappa: 83.8 km

Delta to Epsilon: 40.3 km

Theta to Iota: 69.6 km
Theta to Kappa: 62.2 km
Theta to Lambda: 125.1 km
Iota to Kappa: 34.0 km
Iota to Lambda: 84.1 km
Kappa to Lambda: 64.9 km

Due to a permanent infrastructure limitation, no direct transit corridor exists between Warehouse Alpha and Warehouse Beta.
Furthermore, owing to a regulatory scheduling conflict, the audit route must incorporate exactly one of the following two key corridors: the link between Warehouse Beta and Gamma, or the link between Warehouse Gamma and Delta.

The objective is to determine the minimal total travel distance for a closed circuit that visits each warehouse exactly once, commencing and concluding at the same facility.
